items.text: `parse()` in `src/index.ts` tolerates leading and trailing whitespace by calling `str.trim()` before the regex match (fixed 2026-11-03 in commit `a98ae00` on `feat/compound-format`, not pushed; commit co-authored with Claude). `' 2d'` gives 172800000 and `'1.5h '` gives 5400000; previously such input, common from YAML configs, returned NaN. The length check still runs on the original string, so a whitespace-only value like `'   '` returns NaN rather than throwing. A test was added in `src/parse.test.ts`; only that file was run (41 tests passed), not the full suite.

Compound mode of the short formatter (`format(5400000, { compound: true })` returns `1h 30m` instead of `2h`) was specified by the user on 2026-11-03 with these rules: largest unit first, zero parts skipped, parts separated by a space, smallest unit is seconds (leftover milliseconds dropped), days is the top unit (no weeks/months/years, so 400 days gives `400d`), negative values get a leading `-` (e.g. `-1h 30m`). It was implemented in commit `5247e1b`, which emits the `1d 1h 30m` style.

A compound option was added to the short formatter (5247e1b): format(5400000, { compound: true }) returns "1h 30m", largest unit first, zero parts skipped, days to seconds only, leftover ms dropped. | When: 2026-11-03 | Involving: Bench User

items.text: Early ms history (2012–2015): the project began with an 'Initial import as repository' (eb10804) by Guillermo Rauch on 2012-03-07, followed by a mocha fix and a performance contribution by tubalmartin (a3259a5, 2.8x better performance with a smaller footprint). 0.4.0 added rounding to fix crazy decimals; 0.5.0 made short formatting the default and added a .long option (8263f19); later 0.5.x added a license and reused helper variables in parse. 0.5.1–0.6.2 (2013) fixed a minutes bug caused by a badly named variable (#22, 9992f8a), fixed singularization, and added a repository field to package.json. 0.7.0 (2014-11-24) and 0.7.1 (2015-04-20) added time abbreviations, a LICENSE file, a license field in package.json (for License Finder), and a guard against extraordinarily long inputs (@evilpacket).

items.text: Revised decision (2026-11-03): the compound duration output must be compatible with Go's `time.ParseDuration`: parts glued together with no spaces and hours as the largest unit (e.g. `25h30m`), replacing the earlier `1d 1h 30m` style with spaces and a `d` unit. Reason: deploy logs are scraped by a Go service that runs every duration through `time.ParseDuration`, which rejects spaces and has no `d` unit. Not yet implemented: still to do on `feat/compound-format`, where commit `5247e1b` still emits `1d 1h 30m`. This supersedes the earlier space-separated, days-as-top-unit rules.
